reviews.text: I bought both my eldest and second children here. The staff is incredibly kind; thank you so much! 🥹 …

My regular veterinarian told me that dogs purchased here don't have microchips, and that this could cause problems later on, so I decided against buying a dog here.

A Chinese owner I spoke to had apparently bought a dog here, and was told at the reception desk to inquire with the pet shop about whether the dog had a microchip.

I recommend that Japanese people go to a trustworthy shop, even if it costs a little more.

I had made a reservation to see a Maltipoo recently. Despite a typhoon, I traveled all the way from Saitama to Higashi-Shinjuku.

However, even an hour before my arrival, I received no notification that the puppy had already been sold. I was shocked that there was no prior contact, especially since I was on my way to the store.

I had made a reservation, so why couldn't they have informed me earlier? I felt this was incredibly inconsiderate of a customer who had traveled a long distance and incurred significant travel expenses during a typhoon.

Furthermore, even after entering the store, no staff members came out for quite some time, and I was very concerned about the hygiene of the store. The smell, in particular, was extremely strong; honestly, I found it difficult to stay there for even a short period.

I've been to many pet shops before, but this was my first time visiting a pet shop run by Chinese owners, and it was the first time I'd had such an unpleasant experience.

The cat I adopted from this shop previously had a skin disease and ear mites that weren't mentioned at the time of sale. Fungi are mold, right? Mold shouldn't grow on a cat's body unless the environment is extremely bad. There were several spots all over its body. I've adopted and raised several cats from various shops before, but this is the first time something like this has happened. I'd like to know how they managed to raise a cat to end up like this. The response was also unsatisfactory.

The shop smells terrible, and there are no staff members who can speak proper Japanese. It's a wonder they're still in business in this state. Please close down.

The smell was terrible the moment I walked in.
It was a little hot, but the air conditioning wasn't on at all.
The toilets were dirty but left unattended.
It's a terrible environment for Japan, and I feel sorry for the residents.

I got a cat from this pet shop.
When I bought it, I noticed hair loss on its tail and the clerk explained that it had been fighting with other cats and had become bald due to stress.
When I bought it, I realized it didn't have a microchip so I took it to a nearby vet who also got it vaccinated.

When I brought it home, it was sneezing and had a runny nose, so I took it to the vet again to have it checked for hair loss, which was diagnosed as rhinitis and fungal hair loss.
When I called Maneki Neko later, they said they couldn't give me a refund but would give me one free shampoo to treat the fungal infection.
However, Maneki Neko called me back later and said they would give me a full refund.
When I went back the next day and asked about a refund, they said they couldn't refund the initial consultation fee or the prescription fee for the rhinitis medication, but they would only refund the cost of the fungal treatment and, mysteriously, the follow-up consultation fee. (One of the antifungal medications was also missing.)
When I asked if the rhinitis had been present since the pet shop, the clerk seemed to have been on the phone with the owner, and handed me the phone and spoke to me over the phone. When I signed the contract, they asked if the dog had been sneezing, and I told them I hadn't seen anything, but they insisted that they hadn't seen any symptoms at home. I wasn't willing to budge, so we argued on the phone for about an hour, and the owner said they would check the security cameras and check with the veterinarian at the animal hospital where the dog had been infected, and then call me.
When I went to the animal hospital the other day to check, they said they had received a call from Maneki Neko.
The veterinarian explained to me that "Based on the severity of the symptoms, it's likely that the dog had been suffering from the condition for some time, rather than something that would develop immediately after adoption."
However, it seems they were unwilling to acknowledge the possibility that the condition had been present since before the purchase, citing the reason that "no such symptoms were mentioned during vaccination."

I believe they have confirmed this. When will you call me?

If you are considering adopting a pet, I strongly recommend thoroughly checking the dog's health and warranty details.

I'm posting this for anyone considering going to this salon. My dog ​​suffered a serious injury during a grooming session here in September 2025. My monthly regular groomer was fully booked, so I went here for the second time last month. Immediately after the grooming session, the dog's red, abraded skin was completely exposed. (The scab in the bottom center shows the scab five days later.) After cutting the dog's fur, the wound appeared from the inside. (Even though I trim the hair to 1cm length once a month.) The doctor said the redness was caused by shampoo seepage. The groomer didn't even show up, just explained the situation at the reception desk. The next day, the dog was examined by a veterinarian, and I received a diagnosis that the clippers were used during the grooming session. I sent the documents by certified mail, but no response was received within the deadline. When I called, the owner (a Chinese woman in her 30s) insisted that she had been to China and didn't know when she would return. The groomer in question has sensitive skin, right? However, when I visited the store, the owner was there (the previous time I went to negotiate, he said he was the owner and asked me to bring the medical certificate), and when I confronted him about it, he said he wasn't the owner, that the medical certificate was probably fake, and that he hadn't seen the certified letter...I'm shocked. Thinking about how scary and painful this must have been for my child, I will never forgive him.

I went to get my dog ​​groomed the other day.
When I picked him up, he looked completely different from the style I had requested. The staff's attitude was also incredibly bad.
There were many patches of hair that had not been trimmed. He seemed listless when we got home, and I wonder how they had groomed him. It was the first time I had ever seen him look like that, and I was very shocked.
He had been shaved so unevenly that you could see his skin in places. The hygiene in the store was also poor, and the smell was awful. The cages of the dogs for sale were covered in feces and had not been cleaned up. His bellies were red. I really can't believe it. I'm disappointed.
I would never recommend going there.
I will never forgive this.
The hygiene doesn't seem very good.

We recently welcomed our third adorable cat into our family from this shop!

The staff were incredibly kind and helpful, giving us detailed advice on everything from the new cat's personality and health to tips on how to get her to get along with our two existing cats.

The cat is energetic and curious, and quickly became a part of our family after we brought her home. We've been so grateful for their willingness to patiently answer any questions or concerns we have about raising a cat.

With our third cat, our family's happiness has increased even more! We look forward to continuing to rely on your services! Thank you so much!
